prompt: ECMA-262 ForDeclaration BoundNames forbidden string syntax error
answer:
The rule means that a **bound name whose value is the string `"let"`** is forbidden in a `for…in` or `for…of` declaration:

```js
for (var let of iterable) {} // SyntaxError
```

ECMA-262 lists this early error:

> It is a Syntax Error if the BoundNames of `ForDeclaration` contains `"let"`.

It also separately forbids duplicate bound names and conflicts with names in the loop body’s `VarDeclaredNames` ([ECMA-262 §13.7.5.1 as reproduced by Microsoft](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/ie_standards/ms-es2018/64c34785-1111-1111-849f-a303f847396b)).

This does **not** prohibit an ordinary declaration using `let`:

```js
for (let x of iterable) {} // valid
```

Here, the `BoundNames` contains `"x"`, not `"let"`.

The reason `"let"` is singled out is that it is not treated as a keyword by the lexical grammar; instead, it is treated as reserved through static-semantic restrictions ([Stack Overflow result](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/34317632/why-is-let-singled-out-in-the-for-of-specification)).
